newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil 97/98 coffee crop at best 20 mln bags -coop.
newsitem.headline: Brazil 97/98 coffee crop at best 20 mln bags -coop.

text.p: Brazil's 1997/98 coffee crop will at best reach 20 million 60-kg bags despite earlier expectations the harvest would return to levels seen before the 1994 frosts, said a Minas Gerais cooperative.

"With the frosts of 1994, the expectation was that Brazil would return to normal coffee production....from 1997," said Jose Geraldo Rodrigues de Oliveira, superintendent at the Cooxupe cooperative in Gauxupe, Minas Gerais state.

"But unfortunately that is not going to happen. Everything indicates that the 1997/98 harvest will be much smaller than in 1996. Brazil will produce, under the most optimistic hypotheses, around 20 million bags of coffee," he said.

According to Jose Bras Matiello, national coordinator for Procafe, part of the Ministry of Agriculture, tree stress, weather stress and the effects of a cold winter have contributed to a harvest which he forecasts will reach 19.2 million bags.
Matiello's estimate compares with a forecast of 17.8 million bags issued by cooperatives' associations in the Cerrado region of Minas Gerais at the end of November.

Cooxupe has conducted its own survey of 405 growers covering 25,000 hectares of coffee in the Guaxupe area.

All local districts with the exception of Guaranesia are anticipating a smaller harvest than that of 1996, with output seen at 456,109 bags, down 42.58 percent from the 794,291 bags produced over the same area this year.
An extended period of low temperatures is most likely the principal cause for the large number of abnormal flowerings seen in recent months, according to researcher Alemar Braga Rena.
According to Rena, in June this year, Vicosa in the Zona da Mata region of south Minas Gerais saw 54 days below 10 degrees Celsius in May to September against 37 days in the same period in 1995.
Patrocinio in the Cerrado region saw 72 days below 10 degrees Celsius against 48 days in 1995.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
